caption: What if you painted the Diwali sky? Every firework colour comes from a burning metal. Heat kicks the metal's electrons up, and as they fall back they give off light in that element's own colour. Strontium makes red, calcium orange, sodium yellow (the glow of old sodium street lamps), barium green and copper blue. Blue is the hardest: its copper compound breaks apart above about 1,200 °C. Mix strontium and copper and you get purple. Over 85% of India's fireworks are made in one town, Sivakasi in Tamil Nadu. Plot twist: in 1868, during a total eclipse seen from Guntur, India, the Sun showed a bright yellow line right next to sodium's. It was a new element, helium, named after the Sun and found on Earth 27 years later. Celebrate safe: a sparkler burns over 1,000 °C, so light at arm's length, keep a bucket of water nearby and never relight a dud. Which colour would YOU paint the sky? 👇
